market_question: Will Renan Santos finish in second place in the first round of the 2026 Brazilian presidential election?
reasoning: Renan Santos is a low-visibility candidate from the MBL movement with negligible national polling. Historically, second place in Brazilian presidential first rounds is held by established major-party figures like Lula or Bolsonaro, not third-party activists. Unless a massive realignment and split of the main right-wing vote occurs in his favor, his probability is realistically around 1-2%. The market's 6.5% looks like noise-driven overpricing.
evidence_points: No second-place finisher in modern Brazilian elections has been a non-traditional, minor-party candidate without major party backing.
Renan Santos's MBL lacks the organizational reach and funding of PSDB, PT, or the Bolsonaro movement.
Early 2026 speculation centers on Lula and Tarcísio de Freitas; Santos is not mentioned in any credible frontrunner discussions.
sources_consulted: General political knowledge of MBL and Renan Santos
Early 2026 candidate speculation in Brazilian media (e.g., Folha, Estadão)
